title: Offline Coordinate Card: Field-Ready Summary
description: Copy a clean coordinate and address summary for field notes with the Offline Coordinate Card — no account, no sync, works offline. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a surveyor's day ends with a pocket of these cards — point, coordinates, address — that survive dead batteries and absent signal, because paper and plain text do not need a network.
quick_answer: The Offline Coordinate Card copies a clean summary of a point — coordinates and address fields — formatted for field notes, with no account or cloud sync. Locate the point, copy the card, and file it with your notes: the card is text, and text works everywhere, including offline.

faq: Does it sync to the cloud?
No — deliberately. The card is copied text; your notes app, notebook or glovebox is the storage, under your control entirely.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — build cards for any point you locate on the map; your own location is only used if you ask for it.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
The address fields come from open geocoding data; other sources may record the same point's address differently.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
Clean text, laid out for notes — copy and paste anywhere. Print it and it is a paper card, the original offline technology.
One card per point, pasted in sequence — a field log emerges from the repetition.
Can I add my own notes to it?
Once copied, the text is yours — annotate freely. The card is a starting format, not a locked form.
Does it work with no signal?
The copied card, yes, forever. Making a new card needs the page loaded — open it before the dead zone and it serves the day.
WGS84 coordinates at the precision the located point carries — the same standard as the rest of the site.
